method:
Character library on a real loopback origin, isolated native browser profile.

The initial legacy world is a labelled command-earned pursuit checkpoint. UI
actions create/import/switch/delete characters. Boundary failures are explicitly
injected; accelerated simulation is not a human pacing or performance test.

Old single-character save remains the default until an explicit action
Existing partial project loads from the accepted save
Existing character appearance is set through accepted rules
Character library is discoverable from More and its own tab
Existing card shows actual level, weapon, and pinned project
Empty name cannot create a character
Legacy library permits importing a separate character
Naming and Tab focus do not fire attacks or change cameras
Typing a valid name enables creation without losing the input
Explicit creation selects a second identity
New character has the selected real appearance
New character receives no old gear, XP, notes, or project progress
Creating a library leaves original browser save bytes intact
New character starts in third person independently of the prior tactical view
Switch clears combat, build, selection, and music runtime
New character can edit its own real music score
A delayed audio export cannot export the newly selected character by mistake
A pending score import cannot write into a newly selected character
A pending character import cannot open a preview after switching lives
Refused delayed character import retains the selected world and saved bytes
Switch restores original partial survey and owned equipment exactly
Original notebook and score remain separate

Browser loads exact regenerated HTML
